hypothesis: If the coherent I009 thermal multiplier identifies a real common free-strain defect, applying that benchmark-derived coefficient in a non-production diagnostic profile will improve L20 while leaving L19 exactly unchanged.
predictedSignature: L19 actual physical rows remain numerically identical because the diagnostic changes thermal strain only.
L20 restraint and source-end-action failures decrease materially if thermal free strain is a dominant cause.
A displacement/rotation regression remains a rejection signal even if restraint counts improve.
The fitted coefficient remains productionAuthority=false and cannot become a committed material constant without independent CAESAR/material authority.
mechanicsDelta: No production mechanics change. The workflow generates a temporary diagnostic profile using I009's gravity-weighted median implied coefficient 1.2231989412028551e-05 1/K, runs the exact baseline solver against the locked ACCDB, and discards that coefficient as production authority.
decisionReason: Corrected locked run 31303734798 produced A/B evidence fnv1a64:854f2715892eb74f. All 2340 L19 physical rows were exactly unchanged. L20 restraint failures improved 5->2 and source-end-action failures 137->43, proving thermal free strain is a major causal contributor. However L20 displacement/rotation failures worsened 72->80 and two restraint failures remain. The benchmark-derived coefficient is therefore not an acceptable fix and remains diagnostic-only.
